_comment: claude-hub project permissions. Phase 1.5 of --dangerously-skip-permissions migration (Issue #53). Phase 1 (initial allowlist) was too restrictive for /pdca workflow — read-only commands (cat/head/tail), runtime invocations (bash/bun/node/python/npx), and broader git operations (diff/show/log/checkout/stash/commit/push) are now allowed. Destructive ops (sudo/rm-rf/dd/mkfs), network exfil (curl/wget/nc/ssh/scp), and shell injection (eval/exec) remain denied. The hijoguchi Bot (scripts/start-hijoguchi.sh) auto-loads this file because its CWD = claude-hub root. Phase 2 will flip CLAUDE_HUB_UNSAFE_SKIP_PERMISSIONS default from 1 to 0 and the allow/deny entries below become the active policy.
_known_limitations: In enforce mode the deny list is best-effort; Claude Code's allow/deny patterns are matched before shell expansion, so `rm -rf ~/foo` (tilde literal) and `rm /Users/...` (absolute) require separate patterns. Tighten per Phase 2 review before flipping the default. `Read` deny rules cover file-reading via the Read tool. `Bash(curl:*)` etc remain denied even though scripts that internally call curl (e.g. pushover-notify.sh) work because the parent `Bash(bash:*)` invocation is what's matched, not the child curl process.
